science.title: TiN/dielectric nanolaminates: effects of metamaterial engineering and disorder on the superconductive properties
science.description: A series of TiN thin films and TiN/TiO2 and TiN/AlN nanolaminates were deposited using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) to study whether the previously demonstrated metamaterial approach to enhancing the superconductive properties of layered (i.e. hyperbolic meta-) materials is relevant to TiN. While none of the nanolaminate multilayers had superconducting transitions, Tc, that exceeded the bulk value of TiN, there were enhancements compared to the Tc’s of very thin single layer films (thinner than 30 nm) of comparable thicknesses, which have reduced values due to the effects of disorder. Upon closer examination, it is apparent that the nanolaminate stacks do not behave like individual superconducting layers separated by dielectric layers, but rather as an anisotropic single layer which results in higher Tc’s than for single layer superconductors. We discuss the role of the metamaterial engineering approach for hyperbolic superconductors versus other possible mechanisms of Tc enhancement and effects of disorder.
